audit_scope: Dan Hallagan / Kayenta Obsession second-edition base/core standard 16-round 2–4-player multiplayer, base objective deck; all marked expansions and optional variants excluded.
decision_basis: No material gameplay error or important omission found after direct primary-source comparison. One nonmaterial verification-date metadata inconsistency is recorded.

findings.issue: The verification date predates the cited 2026-10-06 corrigendum and the 2026-11-05 summary date, so it does not describe verification of this exact source/version snapshot.

source_evidence.evidence: Front matter gives summarized_date 2026-11-05 and rulebook_version citing Corrigendum 1.0 2026-10-06.

findings.recommendation: Update verification_date when recording verification of this exact snapshot. This does not affect gameplay or scoring.

checked_claim_groups.assessment: The summary consistently selects the four base families, base tiles/gentry/objectives, standard 16-space board and 2–4-player multiplayer. Marked expansions and optional modules, including Hiring When Passing and replacement objective decks, are excluded. Verification-date inconsistency is nonmaterial and recorded below.

Random first player; family selection begins on their left clockwise; 1.1 baseline and Cavendish 1.4; five available starting servants; five unupgraded starter tiles; four family cards with Asquith Dowager; two starter guests and unused starters reshuffled; five secret objectives; Ponsonby £300; York extra footman all agree.

source_evidence: Universal pp. 10–12; original p. 12 Alderley Hall illustration
checked_claim_groups.assessment: Hire supply has one valet/maid and two footmen per player plus two total underbutlers. Use player count plus one double-sided monuments and at most one Estate monument. Initial six distinct eligible tiles use PR<=3, exclude Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments, stack duplicates, sort numbers, orient normal/hybrid tiles correctly. Reveal first theme and prepare Fairchilds.

source_evidence: Universal pp. 16–21; original p. 12 Alderley Hall illustration
checked_claim_groups.assessment: Twelve player turns; no turns/rotation/ongoing income at courtship. Host and pass sequences agree. Track events precede ongoing tile effects. The original board confirms Village Fairs at 3/9, Draw Objectives 6, Builders’ Holiday 11, National Holiday 14 and courtships 4/8/12/16. Only the last player advances the round marker.

Exact gentry count/type from hand, family eligibility for Ladies/Gentlemen, service for every tile/card icon, inability to host requiring pass, positive-before-negative mandatory favours, optional dismissals, and cleanup destinations/mandatory upgrades agree.

Wheel increments versus levels, minimum 1.1, maximum Max.5, fixed screening level at end of step 2, acquisition/scoring independent of PR, National Holiday, overflow use of special actions and money-payment enforcement agree. Special actions have costs 2/3/4 increments; Borrow Money and Service Help repeat; special refresh is once per turn; other refresh methods remain separate.

Common/unique distinction, one unique per type, housekeeper/Brushing Room conditional substitutions, underbutler male substitutions, all used servants expended, Butler’s Room no-gentry hiring and upgraded recruitment, underbutler acquisition exclusively via Pantry into Expended Service, and Quarters tile versus paid Service Help versus Refresh Service agree.

Attendees from hand versus deck-to-hand invite favours, revelation of kept guests only when screening, rejected/dismissed cards to appropriate deck bottom, dismissal from hand/activity/discard, family immunity, unsavoury definition and retention/scoring destinations agree. Family favours/VP, base Fairchild favours/service/type/VP and both base gossips agree.

Mandatory first upgrade, ongoing-only tiles, reminder tokens, hybrid underlined initial side and flip-after-each-use/category-only counting agree. Barn, Servants’ Hall, Private Study and Main Library rules agree. Other base tiles are appropriately governed by their printed requirements rather than duplicated exhaustively.

Heritage doubles all guest favours, Queen doubles one favour, Lionheart draws a prestige guest without personal service and doubles nonnegative favours; both latter suites become monuments. Fixed one-guest requirement, South Lawn Estate five gentry including two family, Long Gallery count reduction, and base West Terrace both-side activity/three-family requirements and upgraded draw-plus-optional-dismissal agree.

One normal purchase, market-space price plus modifier, £100 floor, no duplicates by any means, Reserve £300 plus modifier with every tile accessible, Service then PR1 opening and Largest Wine Cellar exception, refill sliding/duplicates/new-only sorting and Reserve routing agree.

Refresh removes market tiles temporarily, leaves Reserve, draws/sorts six then returns removed tiles. Seasonal refresh is the current default. Builders’ Holiday and Market Purchase share multiple-purchase rules: unchanged market/prices and no intermediate refill/refresh. Multiple VP refreshes plus other refresh methods are supported.

Five initial plus round-six two objectives, one discard at every courtship including final, shuffled simultaneous discards to objective-deck bottom, extra objectives increasing final retained count, and tile ownership rather than upgrading agree. All printed VP-card benefits, immediate or own-turn use plus final chance, bottom-deck discard, and benefit-versus-VP choice agree.

Return Fairchilds; current theme scoring including negative VP/current hybrid category; winner/tie awards; objective discard; Reserve then refresh then theme then anticlockwise first-player transfer and round advance agree. Final courtship counts all four themes including repeated categories, breaks highest-score ties by reputation level only, then gives final special-action/VP-use opportunity.

All printed tile and hand/discard gentry VP, retained objectives/cards, reputation 1/3/6/10/15/21/28, two VP per servant, £200-floor wealth scoring, and Fairchild then reputation-level then shared-victory tie rules agree.

source_evidence: Universal pp. 106–111; French publisher base rules pp. 7 and 14 only for maximum-reputation objective
checked_claim_groups.assessment: All 30 base-deck objective entries are represented: ten named tile groups, two guest bonuses, five category bonuses, six servant bonuses, four individual tile bonuses, reputation, monuments and wealth. Named tile sets and VP match. Category bonuses include monuments; suites keep categories; hybrids use face-up category. Basic servants exclude unique servants. French p.14 maximum-level/Max-counter example plus p.7 Max=7 clarifies the unchanged reputation objective without importing old gameplay flow.

primary_evidence_highlights.evidence: Standard seasons comprise three game rounds and a courtship; no player turns during courtship; passing refreshes all service and returns discard before round/ongoing effects.
At the end of Step 2, reputation level for screening purposes only is fixed for the rest of the turn.
Current end-of-season order explicitly includes Refresh Market; Builders’ Holiday and Market Purchase finish purchases from a single unchanged market before refilling.
The Seasonal Flowchart player aid is incomplete because it omits the now-default seasonal market refresh; use compendium page 23.
Base basic-servant bonus counts only valets, lady’s maids and footmen.
P.14 says the example reaches the maximum reputation level, as indicated by the Max counter; p.7 identifies Max as level 7 in standard play.
